q: What do we know about feat-cc-dispute-link-v2 in the complaint-classification project?
a: feat-cc-dispute-link-v2 counts disputes opened on or before the ticket date, within 30 days before it. It replaces v1, whose +0.14 macro F1 gain was mostly leakage. On holdout-2025q4 v2 adds +0.03 (0.74 to 0.77, exp-204, 2026-05-12).

q: What came of exp-205 in complaint-classification?
a: exp-205 (2026-03-03) relabelled 1,240 split-billing training tickets and lifted the split-pair macro F1 on holdout-2025q4 from 0.52 to 0.71. That produced fnd-cc-taxonomy-drift, which led to dec-cc-taxonomy-split and the cc-ft-v2 model.

q: What does cc-ft-v2 in the complaint-classification project depend on?
a: cc-ft-v2 is a fine-tuned encoder trained on the adjudicated ds-cc-qa-labels under taxonomy v3, with the 1,240 relabelled split-billing tickets. Its classifier head concatenates feat-cc-dispute-link-v2 to the pooled text vector.

q: What is the current complaint classifier in the complaint-classification project?
a: cc-ft-v2, the fine-tuned encoder with dispute link v2 and split billing labels, which supersedes cc-ft-v1. It scores macro F1 0.84 on holdout-2025q4 (n = 1,800), and tickets are auto-coded only above 0.95 precision under dec-cc-auto-threshold.

q: What share of tickets does cc-ft-v1 auto-code at 0.95 precision in the complaint-classification project, and on which eval set?
a: 58 percent of tickets (1,044 of 1,800) on holdout-2025q4, measured in exp-206 on 2026-02-20.

q: Why did the complaint-classification project drop dispute link v1?
a: v1 joined disputes opened after the complaint, which the complaint itself often triggers, so its +0.14 macro F1 gain was leakage. After exp-204 (2026-05-12) showed the leak, dec-cc-drop-dispute-v1 (2026-05-20) replaced v1 with v2, which uses only disputes opened on or before the ticket date.
